bullets.title: META Iris chip: AVGO +3.8%, NVDA/AMD reliance cut, $10B Canada DC
bullets.body: Meta will begin production of its custom 'Iris' AI chip in September 2026, targeting 14GW of compute capacity. The chip is being designed with Broadcom (AVGO, initial commitment >1GW, multi-year multi-gigawatt rollout) and manufactured at TSMC. META shares fell ~3.7% pre-market as the news signals reduced reliance on NVIDIA and AMD; AVGO rallied ~3.8-5%. Meta is also investing ~$10B in its first Canadian data center.

bullets.title: CRM downgraded to Sector Weight at KeyBanc; Agentforce adoption weak
bullets.body: KeyBanc's Jackson Ader cut CRM from Overweight to Sector Weight (PT removed), citing consistently weak Agentforce customer checks, CIO survey headwinds (Salesforce cited most for budget cuts), and customer data not ready for meaningful AI work. CRM fell ~4.8% pre-market. The note argues any meaningful Agentforce acceleration is further out than consensus models assume.

bullets.title: Semiconductor rally: MU +5.9%, MRVL +5.7%, ALAB +5.0%, COHR +4.9% on AI demand confirmation
bullets.body: Broad AI infrastructure rally overnight driven by Meta Iris news, AMAT CEO citing 2-year demand visibility (some customers through 2030), and reports of NVIDIA H200 chip sales to China (NVDA +4%). Memory names led (MU +5.9%, WDC +5.8%, SNDK +5.4%, STX +5.3%) alongside optical/connectivity names (AAOI +6%, ALAB +5%, COHR +4.9%, LITE +4.4%, MTSI +4.2%, CRDO). Analyst consensus: semiconductor momentum pullback was technical, not a shift in AI capex fundamentals.

bullets.title: MSFT, NOW, ACN, INTU hit on Starbucks AI tool build-out replacing vendor software
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Starbucks is using AI to develop internal tools that replace Microsoft inventory tracking and IBM maintenance software, targeting launch by end of 2027. MSFT -2.1%, NOW -4.4%, ACN -2.6%, INTU -2.5% in pre-market. GS TMT notes MSFT faces three concurrent headwinds: sustained elevated capex, memory pricing exposure via NVIDIA, and potential Office 365 disruption from AI competitors.

bullets.title: NVDA: China H200 approval (capped <200K, training-only) drives +4% pre-market
bullets.body: Reports indicate China may allow NVIDIA H200 imports capped below 200K units with a training-only restriction, driving NVDA +4% pre-market. Separately, JPM credit downgraded MSFT (only hyperscaler not tapped bond markets for capex) and META on heavy supply risk and unclear AI ROIC path. NVIDIA Rosa CPU (2028) expected to use TSMC A16 with back-side power delivery.

bullets.title: TSMC 2Q26 preview: Jefferies expects beat, 30-35% FY revenue growth, Arizona ahead of schedule
bullets.body: Jefferies expects TSMC's July 16 2Q26 print to beat on stronger AI demand, resilient CPU orders, and FX tailwinds, with gross margin expanding to 67.1%. TSMC may guide 3Q revenue +10-12% QoQ vs. Street's high-single-digit expectation and lift full-year growth outlook to 30-35%. Arizona Phase 1 gross margins already ~50% with yields near 90%, ahead of schedule. Key watch: language around supply-demand balance from C.C. Wei.

bullets.title: HPE: Buy reiterated; AI network orders +20% YoY, $2B cumulative; Juniper synergies ahead of plan
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on HPE following investor meeting: orders momentum +20% YoY far outpacing revenue, cumulative AI networking order growth ~$2B, and Year 1 Juniper integration synergies ($200M+) tracking ahead of plan. AMD Helios rack flagged as scale-up upside. Enterprise moving from AI evaluation to deployment phase; supply remains the gating factor.

bullets.title: DELL, HPE, ANET, CLS, CSCO: Agentic AI driving strong upward revisions in Data Center Switch demand
bullets.body: JPM/650 Group discussion identifies agentic AI as a durable multi-quarter demand driver, with DELL and HPE orders expected to grow every quarter. Data Center Switch demand revised up materially for ANET, CLS, CSCO, HPE. CLS flagged as better insulated from silicon constraints due to its well-ordered customer base; CSCO has internal silicon advantage. Storage is the notable laggard as budgets crowd toward compute/networking.

bullets.title: Citi CIO Survey: IT budgets +3.3% NTM; MSFT top AI spend beneficiary, CSCO/DELL cut
bullets.body: Citi's 2Q26 CIO survey (N=100) shows NTM IT budget growth accelerating to +3.3% from +2.6% in March, 0.8pp above the 7-year average. Data/AI is the top investment priority at ~6.5% of IT budgets. MSFT is the top vendor CIOs plan to increase AI spend on, followed by AMZN and GOOGL. CSCO, DELL, IBM, and NOW were most cited for AI spending cuts. 50% of CIOs expect AI to drive headcount reduction in 6-12 months; 24% of AI use cases now in production (up from 22%).

bullets.title: NFLX: Citi cuts PT to $100 from $115 but maintains Buy ahead of July 16 earnings
bullets.body: Citi reduces NFLX PT to $100 (from $115) reflecting 25x 2027E EPS (from 28x) on subdued sentiment, tepid engagement, and M&A fears, but maintains Buy. 2Q26 expected in-line with guidance (~$12.57B revenue, $0.78 EPS). FY26 on track for $51.6B revenue/$16.3B operating income. Piper reiterates OW at $215 PT on Reddit Games (RDDT) strategy separately.

bullets.title: FIG (Figma) 2Q26 preview: JPM cuts PT to $28 from $42 on AI compute margin headwind
bullets.body: JPM forecasts FIG 2Q revenue of $359M (+44% YoY) vs. company guidance $349M, but cuts PT to $28 from $42 as AI-driven compute consumption compresses gross margins to ~81.5% (vs. ~90% in 2Q25). NDR expanded to 139%. Partner checks confirm Figma remains central to design workflows, but Make faces competition from Claude Design and Cursor for prototyping. Citi also flags FIG as a top software pick alongside MDB, SNOW, PLTR, MSFT, SHOP.

bullets.title: PLTR, MDB, SNOW: Citi top software picks into 2Q26 earnings; AI data infrastructure winning
bullets.body: Citi's 2Q26 software preview identifies MDB, SNOW, and PLTR as top earnings setups, driven by AI-concentrated IT spending in cloud/data infrastructure. Traditional application software (CRM-type) faces consolidation pressure and ROI scrutiny. FIG and SHOP also cited as application-layer picks. AI recovery is highly selective—not broad-based SaaS recovery.

bullets.title: HUBS: Oppenheimer sees demand normalization, 2Q26 exceeding internal quota
bullets.body: Oppenheimer notes HUBS showing demand normalization with 2Q26 exceeding internal quota targets and improving linearity; AI picking up traction in the product. Rated Outperform. Separately, NOW and CRM are under pressure from both the Starbucks AI-insourcing narrative and the CIO survey showing spending cuts.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD deal faces state AG lawsuits; PSKY -3.6% pre-market, Arete downgrades to Sell ($2 PT)
bullets.body: NY and CA attorneys general expected to file suit next week to block Paramount Skydance's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on job-loss concerns; the deal carries ~$80B in debt. Arete Research downgraded PSKY to Sell from Neutral with a $2 PT (79% downside from $9.75). PSKY fell 3.6% pre-market; FactSet consensus target is $12.08.

bullets.title: BE: Mizuho and MS defend against short report; scandium supply adequate for 5-10 GW by 2030
bullets.body: Both Mizuho and Morgan Stanley addressed the Hunterbrook Media short report on Bloom Energy, concluding concerns are 'mostly overdone.' MS details that BE's scandium supply chain can support up to 25 GW annual capacity (bullish case only requires 5-10 GW by 2030), uses less scandium than bears assumed, has material stockpile and multiple non-China sources, and Brookfield (BIP) is a financing partner—not a customer—with standard product revenue recognition. BE viewed as attractive for AI/data-center customers on speed-to-power advantage.

bullets.title: LYV reiterated Buy ($202 PT) at GS; SPHR Buy raised to $189 PT; MSGE downgraded to Neutral
bullets.body: Goldman reiterates LYV Buy with PT raised to $202, expecting beat-consensus 2Q and double-digit AOI growth in 2026 with Venue Nation expansion. SPHR PT raised to $189 (Buy) on Wizard of Oz attendance confidence and franchise pipeline. MSGE downgraded to Neutral from Buy (PT raised to $82) as GS sees most upside already reflected.

bullets.title: BABA: JPM raises FY27 EPS 2% (first raise since May 2025) on cloud margins, food delivery losses narrowing
bullets.body: JPM raises Alibaba FY27 adjusted EPS by 2%, citing rapid narrowing of food delivery/quick commerce losses, accelerating cloud revenue with sequential margin improvement, and declining All Others losses. 1QFY27 expected to beat. JPM maintains OW and suggests entering into the upcoming earnings print.

bullets.title: NOK vs. CIEN: MS upgrades Nokia to Overweight/Top Pick; optical and IP units accelerating
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgrades Nokia to Overweight (Top Pick, €14 PT), noting it has de-rated from 28x to 20x forward P/E (35% discount to Ciena) despite optical/IP units expected to accelerate from +11% in Q1 to >20% through year-end following the Infinera acquisition. Ciena remains Equal-weight; MS sees Nokia as better risk-reward post 30% selloff despite slower revenue growth (+7% vs. CIEN ~22%).

bullets.title: RDDT: Piper reiterates OW/$215 PT; Games hits 1M subscribers toward 100M DAU target
bullets.body: Piper reiterates Overweight on RDDT at $215 PT, noting the Reddit Games sample has eclipsed 1M subscribers as part of a broader strategy to reach 100M+ US daily active users.

bullets.title: CCL: MS raising FY26 EPS 4% to $2.26 on solid cruise demand; RCL Q2 beat expected but Q3 guide may disappoint
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley channel checks show mainstream cruise demand improving (+5% YoY bookings in some channels) with pricing firming. MS raises CCL FY26 EPS to $2.26 on lower fuel; strong FCF supports ~$9B cash return FY26-29E. RCL expected to beat Q2 (EPS $3.96 vs. guidance $3.83-3.93) but dull Q3 guidance likely offsets. Luxury cruising strongest with +37% YoY in some channels.
